newsitem.title: USA: Rain keeps Nebraska corn, soy harvest at slow pace.
newsitem.headline: Rain keeps Nebraska corn, soy harvest at slow pace.

text.p: Widespread showers and below normal temperatures kept harvesting of corn and soybeans in Nebraska at a slow pace in the week to Sunday, according to the state's Agriculture Statistics Service.

Corn was three percent harvested, up from one percent a week earlier but below the five-year average of 12 percent. Soybeans were two percent combined, down from an average of 24 percent. Data for last week was unavailable.
"Sunshine and warmer weather conditions are needed to reduce grain moisture levels," the report said. Precipitation amounts ranged from traces to 2-3/4 inches.
Corn was rated 88 percent good to excellent, up from 85 percent a week earlier. Soybeans were 87 percent good to excellent, up from 79 percent the previous week.
Wheat sown totalled 56 percent, up from 44 percent last week but down from the five-year average of 83 percent, as wet weather slowed seeding in southwestern and south central counties.
"Adequate moisture supplies should help germination once the crop is planted," the report noted.
Topsoil moisture was 27 percent surplus, 70 percent adequate and three percent short.
